records.derivation: Aryabhatiya Gitika 1 gives 1582237500 eastward Earth rotations and 4320000 solar revolutions per yuga; the implied civil-day count is 1582237500 - 4320000 = 1577917500, so one sidereal rotation is 1577917500/1582237500 mean solar days.
records.citation: Aryabhatiya I.1, trans. W. E. Clark (1930); Moon 57753336 and Earth eastward 1582237500 revolutions per yuga.
records.caveat: The 86164.101... s display value uses 86400 SI seconds per mean solar day as a presentation calibration. Final historical accuracy must compare against an epoch-aware rotation model near 499 CE.

records.derivation: The same yuga contains 1577917500 implied civil days and 57753336 lunar revolutions, giving 1577917500/57753336 mean solar days per lunar sidereal revolution.
records.citation: Aryabhatiya I.1, trans. W. E. Clark (1930): 57753336 revolutions of the Moon and 1582237500 eastward revolutions of the Earth per yuga.
records.caveat: Do not compare only with a J2000 mean lunar period; lunar orbital elements vary secularly and the source epoch matters.

records.text: Daming calendar of Zu Chongzhi; constants transmitted from Song historical calendrical material
records.derivation: The transmitted Daming constants give ji-fa (紀法) = 39491 and sui-yu (歲餘) = 9589, hence 365 + 9589/39491 = 14423804/39491 days per year.
records.citation: 祖沖之曆法 / Daming calendar constants: 紀法三萬九千四百九十一; 歲餘九千五百八十九.
records.caveat: The calendar constant must be compared with the tropical year appropriate to the fifth-century epoch and with the historical day convention, not only J2000.

records.text: Daming calendar of Zu Chongzhi; constants transmitted from Song historical calendrical material
records.derivation: The Daming constants give 月法 = 116321 and 日法 = 3939, so the mean synodic month is exactly 116321/3939 days within this calendrical model.
records.citation: 祖沖之曆法 / Daming calendar constants: 月法一十一萬六千三百二十一; 日法三千九百三十九.
records.caveat: The synodic month varies with epoch; modern comparison must use an epoch-aware lunar/solar ephemeris.

records.text: Yuan Shi 54, Shoushi li jing, bu qi shuo
records.citation: 元史卷五十四, 授時曆經上: 日周一萬; 歲實三百六十五萬二千四百二十五分; 歲周三百六十五日二千四百二十五分.
records.caveat: This is the Shoushi calendrical year constant. It must be evaluated against a tropical-year model at its source epoch, not interpreted as a timeless constant.

records.text: Yuan Shi 54, Shoushi li jing, bu qi shuo
records.derivation: Yuan Shi 54 states 日周 = 10000 and 朔策 = 29日5305分93秒. In this centesimal sub-division, 93 秒 = 0.93 分, so the value is 29 + 5305.93/10000 = 29.530593 days.
records.citation: 元史卷五十四, 授時曆經上: 日周一萬; 朔實二十九萬五千三百五分九十三秒; 朔策二十九日五千三百五分九十三秒.
records.caveat: Historical 秒 here is a centesimal subdivision of the calendrical 分, not the modern SI second. With a display calibration of 86400 SI s/day, one 分 is 8.64 s and one 秒 is 0.0864 s, but those are transformations, not textual identities.
